content.text:
I built `index.html`. It renders with no console errors and no warnings.

**Answer the data gives:** the peak does not come at the same time every year. 11 of the 14 complete seasons peaked in ISO weeks 5–12 (February–March). The 2022/23 and 2023/24 seasons peaked in week 50 (December). The 2020/21 season had no winter peak; its highest week was week 39. The caption states this, and all its numbers are computed from the data when the page loads.

**Layout:**
- **Left, circular view:** one line per ISO year, coloured from 2012 (blue) to 2026 (red) with a legend. Week 1 is at the top and weeks run clockwise. Week and month labels sit around the circle and value rings are labelled. A triangle marks the highest week of each season.
- **Right, linear view:** the whole series on a date axis, in the same year colours. Each season's peak has a triangle and its week number.
- **Linking:** dragging across the linear view highlights that time range in both views and dims the rest. The page opens with the 2022/23–2023/24 range selected, so the static screenshot shows the linking and the two December peaks.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - angle = ISO week (W1 at top, clockwise, 53 slots), radius = consultations per 100,000
  R2: done - one line per ISO year, colour scale by year with legend (2012–2026)
  R3: done - triangle at max week per Saison, computed in JS; also shown in linear view with week label
  R4: done - full weekly series 2012-W40 to 2026-W43 on a UTC calendar axis
  R5: done - brush on linear view highlights selected weeks/peaks in both views, rest dimmed
  R6: done - week + month labels around circle, value rings labelled, year axis, y-axis with unit
  R7: done - title + data-computed caption (most peaks Feb–Mar, two in December, 2020/21 no winter peak)
assumptions:
  - Each ISO week is plotted at its Monday date on the linear axis.
  - Circle uses 53 equal week slots, so W53 has its own position and in 52-week years the circle stays open at W53.
  - A season is "complete" only if it contains week 39 of its second year; the running 2026/27 season is still marked (semi-transparent) but left out of the caption counts.
  - "Late winter" = ISO weeks 1–13 and "December" = weeks ≥48 for the caption's classification.
  - The initial brush selects the 2022/23–2023/24 seasons to show the linking; the user can change it.
limitations:
  - 15 sequential year colours are hard to tell apart; the legend, tooltips and peak week labels help.
  - Year lines in the circle are not joined across the turn of the year (each ISO year is its own line).
  - Month labels around the circle are approximate (mid-month position in a typical year).
  - In the circle, peaks near each other overlap.
```
